49: /**
50:  * Converts a list of controls to treemap leaves.
51:  * Actually a one-to-many mapping since we must make a unique leaf for each nist control on each control!
52:  * @param controls The controls to build into a nist node map
53:  */
54: function controls_to_nist_node_data(
55:   contextualizedControls: Readonly<ContextualizedControl[]>,
56:   colors: ColorHack
57: ): TreemapNodeLeaf[] {
58:   return contextualizedControls.flatMap((cc) => {
59:     // Get the status color
60:     const color = Chroma.hex(colors.colorForStatus(cc.root.hdf.status));
61:     // Now make leaves for each nist control
62:     return cc.root.hdf.parsedNistTags.map((nc) => {
63:       return {
64:         title: cc.data.id,
65:         subtitle: cc.data.title || undefined,
66:         hovertext: cc.data.desc || undefined,
67:         key: control_unique_key(cc) + nc.rawText,
68:         control: cc,
69:         nist_control: nc,
70:         color,
71:         parent: null // We set this later
72:       };
73:     });
74:   });
75: }

77: /** Builds a scaffolding for the nist items using the given root.
78:  * Also constructs a lookup table of control nodes.
79:  * Only goes maxDepth deep.
80:  */
81: function recursive_nist_map(
82:   parent: TreemapNodeParent | null,
83:   node: Readonly<NistHierarchyNode>,
84:   controlLookup: {[key: string]: TreemapNodeParent},
85:   maxDepth: number
86: ): TreemapNodeParent {
87:   // Init child list
88:   const children: TreemapNode[] = [];
89: 
90:   // Make our final value
91:   const ret: TreemapNodeParent = {
92:     key: node.control.rawText || '',
93:     title: node.control.rawText || '',
94:     nist_control: node.control,
95:     parent,
96:     children
97:   };
98: 
99:   // Fill our children
100:   if (node.control.subSpecifiers.length < maxDepth) {
101:     node.children.forEach((child) => {
102:       // Assign it, recursively computing the rest
103:       children.push(recursive_nist_map(ret, child, controlLookup, maxDepth));
104:     });

106: 
107:   // Save to lookup

109:   return ret;
110: }

112: /** Colorizes a treemap based on each nodes children. */
113: function colorize_tree_map(root: TreemapNodeParent) {
114:   // First colorize children, recursively
115:   root.children.forEach((child) => {
116:     if (is_parent(child)) {
117:       colorize_tree_map(child);
118:     }
119:   });
120: 
121:   // Now all children should have valid colors
122:   // We decide this node's color as a composite of all underlying node colors
123:   const childColors = root.children

126:   // If we have any, then set our color
